record.text: On Aug. 10, 2026, the Commissioners Court voted 4-0, with Commissioner Duncan Webb absent, to call an $817.5 million bond election for Nov. 3, 2026, choosing the larger of two final options; with four members present, the unanimous vote included Hill.
On Feb. 23, 2026, he voted with a 5-0 majority to approve a consent agenda that included a construction change order for the jail's medical and mental health expansion.

In August 2021 the Commissioners Court, which he presides over, voted to commit all of the county's roughly $201 million in federal ARPA funds to three public health capital projects, including a medical and mental health infirmary at the county jail; the court documents reviewed do not record his individual vote.

In January 2022 the Commissioners Court approved by majority vote the establishment of the Collin County Mental Health Diversion Program as a mental health specialty court; the order does not record individual votes.

In February 2024 the Commissioners Court, by majority vote with Commissioner Duncan Webb absent, awarded the construction contract for the jail's medical and mental health expansion to Sedalco, Inc.; the order does not record individual votes.

notes.text: County records describe the ARPA-funded jail medical and mental health facility as 125 beds with shell space for 136 more, at a cost of about $112 million, with opening expected in late 2026.

issue_notes.summary: On the bond, Community Impact quoted him saying residents are "going to have to pay the bill, so we want their voice on this decision," and that deferred projects are pushed into the future; Hoodline reported he favored keeping the debt service rate steady.

candidates.background: Michael Slaughter has owned Collin County businesses since 2006, mainly in real estate brokerage, investment, and contracting. He served two terms on the Parker City Council, the second as mayor pro tem, and earlier served on Sachse's animal shelter board and planning and zoning commission. He says he has volunteered for more than a decade as a Collin County reserve law enforcement officer. He is running for the open seat held by Commissioner Cheryl Williams, who did not seek re-election.

notes.text: Says he rose to lieutenant and commanded the Collin County reserve law enforcement unit during more than a decade of volunteer service.

His campaign lists endorsements from the Collin County Deputies Association, the Wylie Police Association, MetroTEX Association of Realtors Advocacy, True Texas Project, McKinney Values PAC, Collin County Conservative Republicans, and Collin County Young Republicans.

candidates.background: Cyndi McCrann Wheless has been judge of the 417th District Court, Collin County's designated juvenile court, since Gov. Rick Perry appointed her in 2004; the Collin County Juvenile Board had appointed her juvenile court referee in 1999. She is board certified in juvenile law. She earned a bachelor's degree in government and politics from the University of Texas at Dallas and a law degree from Southern Methodist University, where she was citation editor of the law review. She previously worked at Haynes and Boone LLP and Wheless & Walker and served as mental health master for the Collin County Probate Court.

record.text: Was appointed to the Judicial Commission on Mental Health in 2018 by the chief justices of the Texas Supreme Court and Court of Criminal Appeals, and to the Texas Juvenile Justice Board by Gov. Greg Abbott in December 2022 for a term ending Feb. 1, 2027.

notes.text: Received the Voice for Children Award from CASA of Collin County in 2006, and in 2022 the Texas Women Lawyers Pathfinder Award and an Award of Excellence from the Collin County Crisis Intervention Team for mental health work.
